business_scope.primary_industry_name: Carbon-Fiber Milling and Brushless Motor Integration of FPV Drones

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Marshall Islands (Unitary National Jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid legal system: statutory corporate law modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law and U.S. common law precedent; Constitution of the RMI preserves Marshallese customary law and traditional land tenure; English is the official legislative language; decisions of the RMI High Court are informed by U.S. jurisprudence.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States of America (1986, as amended 2003)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus), signed June 2017
No comprehensive double taxation agreement (DTA) network; the non-resident tax-exempt regime is treaty-light and relies on statutory exemption rather than treaty relief
U.S.-RMI bilateral economic and technical assistance arrangements under the amended Compact (non-tax treaty, but relevant to foreign investment guarantees)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act 1990 (RMI), as amended (the BCA), including non-resident and tax-exempt provisions; International Business Corporations Act 1990, as amended (available alternative or comparative structure); Money Laundering (Prevention and Control) Act 2010 (MLPCA), as amended, together with the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit (MIFIU) Regulations; Beneficial Ownership Information Regulations 2021 promulgated under the BCA requiring a confidential beneficial ownership register maintained by the RMI-licensed registered agent and filed with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations; Registrar of Corporations Schedule of Fees.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of valid passport for each director, officer, shareholder, and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence; certification of the notary's authority by the competent apostille authority (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State, U.K. FCDO, other Hague Convention competent authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (RMI is a contracting party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961); consular legalization required for documents originating from non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original banker's reference letter or letter of good standing from a recognized financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or financial institution where the principal maintains an account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization where required by the RMI registered agent's AML/KYC policy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential and/or business street address (utility bill, bank statement, or lease) for each principal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank, or licensed landlord
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization as required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized director consent and specimen signature pages, including registered agent engagement letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each proposed director and shareholder; countersigned by the RMI-licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; original wet-ink signatures required for the statutory corporate file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Completed Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and Beneficial Ownership questionnaire with organizational chart, if applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: RMI-licensed registered agent, in coordination with prospective directors and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal compliance document; notarization required only where indicated by the registered agent's risk assessment

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or incumbency for any corporate shareholder entity (certified by its home registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if not issued by an RMI-recognized registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, EU-CFSP Sanctions List, and domestic advisories issued by the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit (MIFIU); PEP status determined per FATF Recommendation 12 and domestic MLPCA implementing rules; the stated FPV drone retail business qualifies for a Low-Risk Standard tier so simplified due diligence (SDD) may be applied, but any PEP, sanctions, adverse media, or high-risk jurisdiction nexus automatically triggers enhanced due diligence (EDD); continuous transaction monitoring is required through the PayPal and Stripe payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (ORC) of the Republic of the Marshall Islands; name reservation is filed exclusively through an RMI-licensed registered agent via the ORC's authorized electronic filing gateway.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the official statutory language; corporate names must be expressed in Roman (Latin) alphabetic characters and must contain a mandatory corporate identifier token (e.g., Corporation, Incorporated, Limited, Ltd., Inc., Corp., or the Marshallese abbreviation 'BC'); Marshallese diacritic characters are permitted but discouraged in the serial-name field; any non-Latin script name must be transliterated and certified, with the transliterated Roman-script version controlling for official registry purposes; the name must be distinguishable upon the register from all existing reserved or registered names and must not misrepresent the corporate nature, public authority, or licensed activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Marshall Islands (without express authorization, where the name falsely implies government connection)
Foundation (where it implies a charitable or public foundation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 30 days from the date of approval and may generally be extended once for an additional 30 days by a timely renewal application filed through the registered agent before expiry. Upon rejection, the registered agent may: (i) request written reasons from the Registrar of Corporations for the adverse finding; (ii) file a written reconsideration request with the ORC within 14 days of the rejection notice, accompanied by a rebuttal memorandum and any amended name variants; (iii) if the reconsideration is denied, institute an administrative appeal to the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands under the Associations Law within 30 days of the denial; and (iv) in parallel, refile a curative name reservation adding a distinguishing element (e.g., a unique identifier or industry descriptor) to secure the incorporation timeline while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office cannot satisfy the statutory registered office obligation. The non-resident Business Corporation must maintain a registered office in the Republic of the Marshall Islands at the physical street address of its RMI-licensed registered agent, with the agent authorized to accept service of process. Remote, cloud-based, and home-office operations for the FPV racing drone e-commerce business (sold via PayPal and Stripe) are fully permissible, and no physical commercial presence in the RMI is required, provided the corporation does not carry on business within the RMI so as to preserve its non-resident tax-exempt status.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5% annual probability) of an unannounced physical on-site inspection of a non-resident, tax-exempt Business Corporation with no domestic RMI operations; however, the probability of documentary AML/CFT and UBO register examination at the licensed registered agent's office is moderate-to-high (approximately 50-65%) within any 12-month supervisory cycle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (ORC)

Beneficial ownership register setup and first-year maintenance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per MLPCA / MIFIU compliance directives

Notarization and Hague Apostille bundle (6 documents)

International courier of original executed documents
Total pre-incorporation cost (standard path, excluding optional expedited fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Sum of statutory tariffs and market benchmarks; optional expedited filing adds USD 200, bringing the fully expedited total to USD 3,085

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act 1990 (as amended), codified at Title 27 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code, ss. 19 (Articles of Incorporation), 23 (Corporate Name), 24 (Bylaws), 44 (Registered Agent), 56 (Board Powers); Foreign Investment Business License Act 1994 (applicable only if local business is conducted)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (with Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of Corporations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; the entity may issue par-value or no-par-value shares with fully or partly paid subscriptions, and capital may be maintained in any currency through non-resident bank accounts
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The share subscriptions set forth in the subscription ledger (including shares issued to the incorporator) are hereby accepted and the corresponding certificate(s) shall be executed and delivered; (2) the registered office of the Corporation shall be established at the address of the registered agent in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands; (3) the following persons are hereby appointed to the offices indicated: President, Secretary, and Treasurer; (4) the Corporation's Bylaws are adopted as submitted; (5) the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, engage counsel, and file all documents necessary to maintain good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance (Majuro counter or authorized online registered-agent portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application with up to two proposed names, pay the USD 50 reservation fee, and obtain written name clearance before filing the Articles of Incorporation. The proposed name must be distinguishable from all existing registered names and otherwise comply with Section 23 of the Business Corporations Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as indistinguishable, file an amended reservation with alternative names; one supplementary submission is permitted without an additional reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and authorized corporate counsel; no governmental filing occurs at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, registered office and registered agent clause, authorized share structure, permitted business purpose (carbon-fiber milling and brushless motor integration of FPV racing drones under ISIC 3240), and the name of the initial director. Prepare Bylaws governing board powers, indemnification, share transfer restrictions, and officer duties.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies are cured by revising the drafts before execution; if a mandatory statutory provision is omitted, redraft the instrument to conform to Sections 19 through 22 of the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (RMI or foreign jurisdiction); apostille or consular legalization where local recording is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each incorporator and the initial director execute the Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws before a notary; affix the corporate seal if adopted. Obtain an apostille or consular authentication where required for overseas banking or registry recognition of the corporate instruments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarization defects are cured by re-execution and re-notarization; if an apostille is inconclusive, obtain a certified notarial copy and, where necessary, consular legalization through the relevant foreign mission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the executed Articles of Incorporation, the name reservation certificate, the registered agent's consent, and the USD 250 government filing fee to the Registrar either in person or through an approved e-filing agent. Upon statutory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation with legal effect as of the filing date.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a correction notice or query, file an amendment to the Articles within the prescribed period (generally 14 days), addressing each stated defect; resubmission is processed without re-imposition of the full incorporation fee in the case of a first query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Statutory Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed resident registered agent, Majuro; Office of the Registrar of Corporations for notice filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered agent's acceptance, establish the registered office at the agent's Majuro address, and open the statutory minutes book, share certificate book, and stock ledger. Ensure that the registered office is available during normal business hours for service of process and official correspondence.
required_dossiers: Stock ledger and specimen share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agent's acceptance lapses or is declined, appoint a substitute resident agent by board resolution and file a notice of change of registered office and agent with the Registrar to maintain good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organization Meeting, First Board Resolution, and Good Standing Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; administrative filings with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold or adopt by unanimous written consent the organizational meeting, approve the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, accept subscription payments, appoint the President, Secretary, and Treasurer, and authorize the opening of bank accounts and engagement of legal counsel. Establish a calendar for annual report and franchise tax filings to preserve good standing.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or unanimous written consent
Annual report and franchise tax filing forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Procedural defects at the organizational meeting are cured retroactively by unanimous written consent of directors and shareholders; late annual report or franchise tax filings are cured by submitting the delinquent filing with payment of the standard fee plus accrued late penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI EPA); Foreign Investment Board for any actual in-country business activity
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No mandatory domestic industrial operating license applies to this non-resident entity because manufacturing, carbon-fiber milling, and drone assembly are performed outside Marshall Islands territory; if a physical facility is later established in the country, an Environment Permit (Title 16 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code) and a General Manufacturing Permit, together with a Foreign Investment Business License, would be required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — non-resident entity has no local manufacturing footprint and no discharge source within the Republic. Any future in-country facility would be classified at a Registration level for small-scale carbon-fiber assembly and light milling, or at a Full EIA Report level if installed capacity, wastewater discharge, or hazardous waste volumes exceed RMI EPA regulatory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Future in-country operations must comply with RMI EPA Water Quality Standards (pH 6.5-8.5; total suspended solids not exceeding 50 mg/L; total petroleum hydrocarbons not exceeding 10 mg/L); VOC and particulate emissions from carbon-fiber milling must be controlled through HEPA and activated-carbon filtration to meet ambient air quality standards; carbon-fiber dust and lithium-polymer battery waste must be handled under an approved solid and hazardous waste management plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the RMI Chief of Fire Safety Services, requiring compliance with NFPA 1 and NFPA 101, including dust-explosion mitigation, fire suppression, and isolated lithium-polymer battery storage; structural load inspection certification for milling machinery; occupational workplace clearance issued by RMI health and safety authorities covering respirator protection, machine guarding, electrostatic grounding, and employee exposure monitoring for carbon-fiber particulates.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (Treasury and Tax Division), Republic of the Marshall Islands; corporate registry administered by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations. No operational online tax filing portal exists; all statutory submissions are made by licensed registered agents, and no electronic TIN issuance platform is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: No statutory TIN or VAT ID is required for a non-resident Business Corporation (BC) because the entity is exempt from Marshall Islands income tax and no indirect tax regime exists. Procedure: (1) engage a licensed registered agent; (2) file Articles of Incorporation under the Business Corporations Act 1990; (3) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the corporate registration number, which serves as the de facto identifier; (4) confirm non-resident domestic corporation status; no separate tax registration step applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (non-resident BC exempt from income tax on all non-RMI-source income; territorial scope limited to income arising in or derived from within the Marshall Islands; no capital gains, withholding, payroll, or property tax at national level)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The RMI does not provide check-the-box, partnership classification, or hybrid mismatch elections under domestic law. The only relevant election is the designation of non-resident status under the Business Corporations Act 1990, which exempts the BC from RMI income tax provided it does not carry on business in the RMI and does not derive income from RMI sources.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None (no VAT, GST, or sales and use tax in the Marshall Islands)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable; no indirect tax registration threshold exists. Customs import duties and a 2% import service charge apply solely to goods entering RMI customs territory and do not affect offshore FPV drone retail sales exported from or transshipped through the RMI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not applicable; there is no e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API integration, or digital stamping mandate in the RMI. Import customs declarations are processed through the RMI Customs Service, and no fiscal clearance or prior approval is required for export transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable; the RMI has no VAT/GST system and therefore no export zero-rating mechanism. Exports of carbon-fiber FPV racing drones, brushless motors, and spare components by a non-resident BC fall entirely outside RMI taxation; no export duty, excise, turnover tax, exchange control, or FX repatriation deadline applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable - no VAT zero-rating claim is possible; retain commercial invoice, packing list, and air waybill as underlying trade evidence
Certificate of Origin (only if demanded by the destination country's customs regime)
Bill of lading or air waybill and freight forwarding records as evidence of physical export movement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT clawback or zero-rating fraud regime exists because no indirect tax is levied. RMI Income Tax Act penalties apply only if a BC loses non-resident status and derives RMI-source income: 10% monthly penalty on unpaid tax plus statutory interest, and willful evasion is punishable by fine up to USD 5,000 and/or up to one year imprisonment. Under the Business Corporations Act 1990, knowingly false statements to the Registrar are subject to monetary penalties and potential administrative dissolution of the corporation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance and Treasury, Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI does not maintain a central bank; the United States dollar is the sole legal tender)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMI has no foreign-exchange control law. Both current and capital account transactions are notionally fully convertible because the domestic currency is the U.S. dollar. There are no statutory exchange permits, profit-remittance approvals, or repatriation limits for non-resident business corporations. Practical convertibility is nevertheless constrained by correspondent-bank AML/KYC requirements, OFAC sanctions screening, and the requirement that funds flow through a licensed RMI banking institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. RMI imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion ratio, or statutory timeline for export proceeds. Export receipts from FPV racing drone sales may be held indefinitely in U.S. dollars or in foreign-currency accounts, subject to the commercial bank's internal transaction-monitoring and documentary trade-support requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI and e-money institutions do not hold an RMI banking license and cannot directly access RMI clearing infrastructure. They may be used only as non-regulated collection front-ends for PayPal/Stripe-style retail receipts, but local banks will ordinarily reject inbound transfers sourced from unlicensed EMIs without full underlying customer and trade documentation. Legal viability is therefore conditional on the EMI maintaining a U.S. or EU bank license and a transparent corresponding-bank trail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permissible for low-risk non-resident business corporations, provided at least one director or authorised signatory completes a video KYC interview and submits apostilled corporate documents, notarised passports, a registered-agent certificate, and a current Certificate of Good Standing. In-person physical appearance is not mandated under RMI banking practice, but the bank retains discretion to require physical attendance where beneficial-ownership documentation is incomplete or where the drone-related trade description creates elevated reputational risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore non-resident corporation with registered-agent postal address, no substantive local physical premises, and tax-exempt status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Certificate of Good Standing and corporate register extract; certified registered-agent engagement letter; apostilled board resolution opening the account and designating signatories; notarised passports of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners; RMI Tax Exemption Certificate; sworn declaration of the company's actual operational base and business substance; audited or reviewed financial statements where available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business keyword 'drone' prompting dual-use, export-control, or arms-trade screening; ambiguous split of PayPal/Stripe payment settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 3240 manufacturing-and-hobby classification letter; product technical datasheet limiting use to recreational FPV racing drones; CE/FCC/RoHS compliance certificates; end-user and end-use declaration expressly excluding military, surveillance, and weapons delivery; supplier list with commercial invoices; payment-provider settlement reports evidencing that funds originate solely from retail e-commerce channels.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be remitted via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the RMI beneficiary bank's U.S. correspondent account in USD. The remittance must carry an appropriate ISO 20022 purpose code, customarily 'CAPC' (capital contribution) or 'INVS' (investment-related transfer), and include a remittance reference stating 'Capital contribution to MH_BC'. Supporting documents required at the receiving bank: board resolution approving share issuance, subscribed share ledger, share certificate, apostilled certificate of incorporation, and a compliance letter from the sending bank identifying each beneficial owner. No RMI exchange-control filing is required because the transfer is USD-denominated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for component purchases and supplier payments shall clear via SWIFT MT103 (standard single payment) and MT202 (bank-to-bank cover) using the RMI bank's U.S. correspondent banking network. For larger or trust-critical transactions, a documentary commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT720) may be issued with transport documents, commercial invoices, and ISIC-aligned product descriptions. PayPal and Stripe retail proceeds are swept in regular cycles into the operational account, then disbursed by MT103 only after OFAC and sanctions screening and after the underlying e-commerce settlement report is retained for audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR outright forwards with a licensed foreign counterparty
USD/CNH outright forwards for supplier settlements in renminbi
USD/JPY outright forwards for brushless motor and carbon-fibre supply chains
Cross-currency interest rate or principal swaps executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with a top-tier non-RMI bank
Non-deliverable forwards for exotic currencies where physical settlement would create unnecessary statutory or operational friction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Annual Return (statement of issued share capital, directors and officers, and registered agent confirmation) covering the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Maritime and Corporate Administrators (Office of the Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before 31 March each year; filing window opens 1 January; no extension is available for non-resident domestic corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty in the form of additional fees per month of delinquency; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off and loss of corporate existence without judicial winding-up

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Renewal Consent (annual declaration of agent consent and office location)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Maintained continuously; agent consent renewal filed concurrently with the 31 March annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of registered agent for more than 90 consecutive days authorizes the Registrar to administratively dissolve the Corporation and revoke the certificate of registration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory external audit for non-resident Business Corporations under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act; an audit becomes mandatory only upon board resolution, demand by shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting shares, or if the entity conducts taxable domestic activity within the Marshall Islands
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or US GAAP permitted; Marshall Islands has no prescribed local GAAP and does not require filing of financial statements for exempt non-resident corporations; books and records must fairly present the affairs of the Corporation and be open to director inspection

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO filing to the Registrar exists under Marshall Islands law; transparency obligations are satisfied by maintaining an up-to-date Register of Members including nominee and beneficial ownership notations, and by confirming any shareholding transfers and officer changes in the annual return; the registered agent must retain current beneficial ownership information for AML compliance and must update the record within 30 business days after any transfer or change
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholder and board proceedings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by law; if voluntarily procured for a compact non-resident entity, USD 5,000 - 12,000 per year

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 3% standard gross revenue tax on RMI-source business revenue; 0% for qualifying non-resident Business Corporations
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory exemption from Marshall Islands corporate income / gross revenue tax for non-resident Business Corporations under BCA Section 68, provided no business is carried on within the Republic; 20-year tax holiday; no capital gains tax, no net income tax, no payroll tax on non-resident employees, and no branch remittance tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Business Gross Revenue Tax Return / Corporate Exemption Declaration (Form GRT-1) filed via the RMI Tax and Revenue Office online portal; non-resident exempt Business Corporations file an Annual Corporate Report with the Registrar of Corporations through the RMI Online Registry instead of a tax return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly installments apply only to entities with taxable gross revenue sourced in the Republic
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For non-exempt businesses: on or before the last day of the month following the close of the taxable year; for non-resident exempt corporations: no tax filing due, but the Annual Corporate Report is due on the registration anniversary date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from sources within the Marshall Islands
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0 or N/A if no RMI-source revenue was derived; maintain documentation showing all sales were concluded outside the Republic and customers are foreign parties
Insert BCA Section 68 exemption reference and attach Certificate of Non-Resident Status issued by the Registrar of Corporations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue tax due at 3% (if Box 1 is positive)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave blank or enter 0 for exempt non-resident entities; any unregistered RMI-source revenue will void the exemption and trigger penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by a director/officer and date signed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The director must certify under penalty of perjury that the corporation remained non-resident and did not carry on business in the Marshall Islands

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of the assessed tax plus monthly interest of 1.5% on unpaid balances; willful false declaration is a criminal offense carrying fines up to USD 10,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years; failure to file the Annual Corporate Report results in administrative dissolution and loss of the tax exemption, with a reinstatement fee of USD 250

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends paid by a non-resident Business Corporation; the Marshall Islands imposes no dividend withholding tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no comprehensive double tax agreements; statutory exemption makes treaty relief unnecessary for RMI tax purposes. Where a foreign jurisdiction imposes withholding on upstream dividends, the shareholder should obtain an RMI Certificate of Tax Residency / Non-Resident Status (Form TRO-Ex-1) from the Tax Revenue Office and submit it to the foreign tax authority to support any available foreign tax credit or domestic law exemption
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% Marshall Islands statutory withholding tax on interest and IP royalties paid to non-residents; no treaty rates apply absent any DTA

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory transfer pricing threshold exists under RMI law; a prudent USD 500,000 annual intercompany transaction threshold is recommended for maintaining arm's-length documentation and economic substance support
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Marshall Islands does not maintain standalone Economic Substance Regulations applicable to qualified non-resident Business Corporations. The non-resident exemption derives from statutory status. However, the Business Corporations Act requires a registered office, registered agent, and adequate corporate records in the Republic. If the entity is managed or controlled from the RMI or carries on business in the Republic, it may be reclassified as resident and become subject to the 3% gross revenue tax and full economic substance scrutiny

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Gross Revenue Tax Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Carrying on tangible business inside the Marshall Islands while claiming non-resident exemption, or knowingly omitting RMI-source gross revenue from a required return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 50% of the tax evaded plus monthly interest of 1.5%; criminal conviction carries a fine up to USD 10,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false exemption declarations or direct the evasion are personally liable for tax and penalties; the corporate veil is pierced and directors may face travel bans, extradition, and custodial sentences

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Entity Without Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the non-resident BC purely as a tax shield with no physical presence, no independent management, nominee directors with no decision-making authority, and no corporate records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative dissolution by the Registrar of Corporations, reclassification as resident with retroactive assessment of 3% gross revenue tax, and fines up to USD 5,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the veil where the shell misleads regulators, creditors, or tax authorities; directors are jointly and severally liable for corporate debts and may be disqualified and imprisoned for fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving high-volume third-party card payments via PayPal or Stripe for FPV drone sales without customer due diligence, source-of-funds verification, or suspicious transaction monitoring as required by RMI AML law and FATF standards
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil fines up to USD 100,000 for compliance failures, suspension or revocation of the company's registration, and referral to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit for criminal proceedings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are subject to personal fines up to USD 25,000; in laundering cases, personal asset forfeiture and imprisonment apply, and travel bans are routinely imposed during investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Representation to Registered Agent / Filing Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting false information in the Annual Corporate Report, concealing ultimate beneficial owners, or supplying forged financial statements to the registered agent or Registrar
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Striking off the company, cancellation of non-resident status, criminal fine up to USD 5,000, and imprisonment up to 2 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute false filings are personally liable for resulting liabilities; criminal falsification enables veil-piercing and restitution orders against personal assets

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a cross-border settlement flow that amounts to money transmission—e.g., collecting customer payments and paying overseas suppliers through pooled accounts—without the required money services business licence in the RMI or the relevant foreign jurisdictions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cease-and-desist orders, fines up to USD 50,000 per violation, asset freezes, and overseas regulatory enforcement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil restitution proceedings in the US, EU, and Asia-Pacific jurisdictions; persistent violations trigger extradition, travel bans, and imprisonment equivalent to wire-fraud charges
